Investing in a sustainable future Exchange Fund Investment Portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050 - Actively expanding the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with a particular focus on climate change and transition prospect considerations - Formulating clear ESG expectations that align with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties to comply - Committing to reducing the Weighted Average Carbon Intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by or before 2030 Supporting regional transition through investments - Continuing to engage with external investment managers to optimize investment opportunities that drive transition - Continuing to explore and prioritize high-quality investment opportunities that can facilitate transition in Asia and generate positive global impacts First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess superior technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not help solve the carbon emission problem. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership to support these industries, the HKMA drives their transition towards sustainable and low-carbon operational practices, thereby bringing beneficial changes to themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, so as to drive comprehensive decarbonization across the broader economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of its portfolio relies not only on the portfolio's own adjustments but also on broad-based economic transition. Although there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA enhanced its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the Exchange Fund and global net-zero targets. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including the integration of ESG factors into fundamental analysis and stewardship, portfolio decarbonization tilts, and thematic investments across various asset classes that align with the pathway towards net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve portfolio tilts towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, there may be a greater focus on investments that facilitate transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continuously identifies investment opportunities that can promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio, with financial performance comparable to relevant portfolio benchmarks (Chart 5). - Public market investments – The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focusing on sustainability and climate transition, and expanded the application of customized low-carbon equity indices to two other portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek Green, Social and Sustainability (GSS) bonds that can provide competitive returns while funding sustainable projects (for relevant case studies, see the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds"). - Private market investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities that align with the themes of climate and energy transition. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA also actively identifies and evaluates investment opportunities that can accelerate energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multinational organizations (for examples, see the section "Collaborating to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Globally"). - Passive portfolios using ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Adopting customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios whose investment benchmarks are not ESG indices - Active portfolios with a governance theme - Active ESG portfolios themed around sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed around energy transition and decarbonization globally, in Asia, and in the Global South - Green, Social and Sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organization - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" program, providing climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-governmental organization. The proceeds raised from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading aging equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects cover the optimization of monitoring and control systems as well as water pump performance, aiming to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to the continuous treatment of wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other building materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize the gases generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond provides funding for multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess water flow from rivers to arid regions. The primary objective of the project is to repair the deteriorating canal lining to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. Furthermore, the project conducts skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and optimal use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA's key focus areas in 2024 to deliver on this commitment was the plan to advance the target timeline for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target, in line with the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and well-being, striving to promote financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the primary decision-making body for various corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee endorsed in October 2024 the HKMA's new target of achieving net-zero emissions for its corporate operations by or before 2030, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda (Action Agenda). At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on the implementation of sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff well-being, and community engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division acts as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Group, comprising staff from different operational departments, provide another layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing recommendations on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its employees, and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" Logo to the HKMA for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to adopt a structure comprising three main pillars: environment, staff, and social responsibility. - Focusing on decarbonisation and digitalisation in the HKMA's daily operations, with the target of achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2030 - Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promoting greener practices to the financial industry and the wider community - Building a motivated workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Fostering a collaborative, caring, and inclusive working environment that values diversity and strengthens staff sense of belonging - Providing a quality working environment and promoting a healthy lifestyle - Cultivating a culture of caring for the community - Incorporating social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management - Promoting financial inclusion and enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education campaigns The HKMA is mindful of climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to advance the target timeline for achieving net-zero emissions in its own corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its original commitment, as part of the Action Agenda. The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards the net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, conserving energy, reducing paper consumption, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging the improvements in the fuel mix for electricity generation by local power companies. In addition, the HKMA has established a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, recognising the importance of cultivating a sustainability culture, the HKMA encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the overarching 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procuring low-carbon products wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from its air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offsetting schemes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting schemes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. Apart from the above environmental commitments regarding physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, ranging from the rollout of electronic document submission and processing procedures to the promotion of e-payments and the collection of coins for recirculation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting staff well-being and caring for the community. Under the HKMA's overarching corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring continuous operations, the design of the HKMA offices incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only the offices but also communication and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to execute contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking the greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption arising from its own operations. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 associated with its corporate operations by or before 2030. These targets were formulated with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi). The HKMA adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's primary greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect emissions resulting from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate the major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills, as well as staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The scope and basis of the agency's verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" appended at the end of this report. The HKMA walks the talk by upholding the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to comply with. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, during various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting-out materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy-saving measures of its offices and data centres, and adopted a modularly designed uninterruptible power supply system in its data centre facility upgrade project in 2024, further optimising the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency at partial loads, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA strengthens internal virtual collaboration through a digital workplace, which, coupled with streamlined workflows, effectively reduces paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the lifespan of mobile and desktop devices with reference to the manufacturers' software update cycles, thereby prolonging the safe usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated in the office, the HKMA adheres to the "4R" principles, namely refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins at various convenient locations in the office to recycle different materials. To boost the recycling rate, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit nets in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Green Event Pledge", committing to adopting measures to reduce waste generated from various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, such as consolidating multiple trips as far as possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing its annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a "Gold Standard" certified carbon offsetting scheme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the scheme focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The HKMA held its inaugural "HKMA Green Month" from Earth Day on 22 April 2024 throughout May, with the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This presented an excellent opportunity to drive the HKMA's commitment and momentum in practicing environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The programme included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to practice green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz, and a Japanese "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop; it also featured the sharing of waste audit results and a presentation on recycling best practices by a community recycling centre operator. To sustain the momentum of the "Green Month", the HKMA launched an approximately six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that collective small changes in individual habits can significantly enhance the overall corporate recycling performance. One of the highlights of the campaign was the launch of the "Green Action" video, featuring several senior executives sharing recycling tips. The campaign also rolled out a series of screensavers, strikingly designed posters, intranet articles, and e-reminders to remind staff to take action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and collect their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help formulate future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as a key agent of change and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition, driving the financial industry and the wider community to adopt sustainable practices. The HKMA has rolled out multiple measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Data Submission Platform (CDSP) in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as Stored Value Facility (SVF) licensees, to facilitate their submission of certain supervisory data. The expansion of the platform's service scope aims to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, providing a smoother experience for all users while reinforcing the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures introduced in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys with a simplified submission process, and the Smart Information and Document Management System, a central platform providing users with advanced search functions for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Data includes the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel for 2024, as well as their respective intensities. In addition, the Data also includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions generated from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, along with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data is compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, of which 5 offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification work was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to their sources; it also reviewed the fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for checking. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work is strictly independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes: - The Data is materially accurate and reliable; - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Sham Siu Yan, Lead Auditor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025.
